title: SBOM
description: A subject's package inventory, such as what a scanner found in the filesystem of a platform manifest: its distribution, and each package with its ID, name, version, type, purl and CPEs. The event's coverage is the producer's: the scanner's is the share of the ELF files that packages own.

packages.description: The packages, each with an ID of its own. Empty when the subject has none.

failedCatalogers.description: The producer's catalogers that failed, whose packages the inventory may lack.

distro.description: The distribution of the subject, as its os-release file names it. Absent when the producer found none.

id.description: os-release's ID, such as debian or alpine.

version.description: os-release's VERSION_ID, such as 12 or 3.22.2. Absent for a rolling distribution.

idLike.description: os-release's ID_LIKE: the distributions that this one derives from.

id.description: The package's ID, unique within the SBOM. A match names its package by it.

version.description: Absent for a package that has none.

type.description: The producer's type of the package, such as deb, rpm, apk, go-module or java-archive.

purl.description: The package URL, with the producer's qualifiers. An OS package's purl names its source package in the qualifier upstream and its distribution in distro, as Syft writes them: a distribution tracks many vulnerabilities by the source package.

cpes.description: The package's CPEs, in the producer's order.

producer.description: What made the inventory, such as Syft at its version.
